US-01
As a restaurant owner, I want my restaurant set up with its name, hours, delivery settings and menu, so that I can take orders on Sufria without engineering work of my own.

The Sufria team runs an onboarding script from one configuration file: name, currency, timezone, opening hours, delivery settings, menu and the first staff account.
The staff password is shown once and stored only as a hash.
Deferred: self-service registration, drafts and the trial status.

US-02
As a restaurant owner or staff member, I want to add, rename, reprice, switch off and remove menu items myself, so that the menu stays accurate without contacting the Sufria team.

An item needs a name of 1–40 characters, a price above zero with at most two decimals, and an existing category; Arabic-Indic digits are accepted.
A switched-off item disappears from the bot's menu and keeps its order history; all switched-off items can be switched on together.
A change that would make the bot's first message exceed 4,096 characters is refused.
A removed item is archived, not deleted, and returns switched off.

Every inbound message is routed to its restaurant by the WhatsApp phone-number identifier, so several restaurants can share one deployment.
Development uses Meta's test number.
Deferred: provisioning numbers through the Cloud API and tracking verification; Meta business verification needs a registered legal entity.

A first message with no active session opens one and sends the welcome with the numbered menu.
A redelivered webhook opens no second session and sends no second menu.
A message during an active session continues at its current step.
Closed (US-23), paused (US-27) or a menu over 4,096 characters: no session is opened.

As a customer, I want to add items by replying with their numbers, so that ordering feels like a normal WhatsApp chat.

Item numbers in Western or Arabic-Indic digits, several in one message, each with an optional quantity.
Each addition is confirmed in one line with the cart's running total; the cart is held in the session.
An unknown number is named and the rest of the message still applies; after three messages in a row not understood, the restaurant's contact number is sent once, if one is set. The cart is never lost.

The summary shows every item, quantity, subtotal, delivery fee and total.
The order is written only on the confirm word; edit returns to the cart, cancel ends the conversation.
Availability is re-checked at confirmation and an unavailable item is removed and named. Prices are not re-read: the price an item had when it entered the cart is the price paid.

The welcome shows my last order that the restaurant accepted, at today's names and prices, unless an order of mine is less than 3 hours old.
Unavailable items are named and left out; when none is available, no suggestion is shown.
Replying with the reorder word fills the cart and goes straight to pickup or delivery, then the summary.

The choice, the address and the fee are recorded on the order.

Built: cash. The order is created at my confirmation with payment pending in cash; no payment question is asked.

US-11
As a customer, I want a WhatsApp message when my order is accepted, ready or cancelled, so that I know what is happening without asking.

Accepted, ready (for pickup, or out for delivery) and cancelled, with the reason when one is given, each send one message; preparing and completed are silent by decision.
Sent at most once: the notifier claims the order before sending; a failed send is retried twice, then logged.
An order older than 23 h 50 min is not messaged: free-form text needs WhatsApp's 24-hour window.

The live list refreshes every 10 seconds while the tab is visible, pauses while it is hidden, and refreshes at once on return.
An order whose status changed in the last 60 seconds pulses.
A lost connection shows a clear warning rather than failing silently.
A history view lists completed, cancelled and expired orders.

One button offers the next valid step; cancelling asks for confirmation and takes an optional reason of up to 300 characters.
